title: ServiceNow, Inc. General SEC Filings
source_summary: Recent NOW SEC filings converted into underwriting-oriented disclosure summaries.

fields.title: ServiceNow, Inc. General SEC Filings
capital_markets_activity: Recent filings include debt issuance and financing-related 8-K disclosure.
capital_allocation_activity: In January 2025, our board of directors authorized an additional $3.0 billion in repurchases under the share repurchase program, and in January 2026, our board of directors authorized an additional $5.0 billion in repurchases under the Share Repurchase Program.
As of December 31, 2025, approximately $1.4 billion of the authorized amount under the share repurchase program remained available for future repurchases.
liquidity_notes: We anticipate cash flows generated from operations, cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities and long-term marketable securities will be sufficient to meet our liquidity needs for at least the next 12 months, although we do expect to seek additional debt financing to fund our acquisition of Armis Security Ltd.
governance_notes: Recent 8-K filings include governance and board composition updates.
controls_and_risk_notes: Our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded, based on the evaluation of the effectiveness of the disclosure controls and procedures by our management as of December 31, 2025, that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level for this purpose.

Factors that might cause or contribute to such differences include, but are not limited to, those discussed in this Annual Report under “Risk Factors” in Item 1A of Part I and elsewhere herein and in other reports we file with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”).
analyst_relevance: Update debt, interest, and refinancing assumptions from disclosed financing activity.
Reflect buyback pace and remaining authorization in share count and capital allocation assumptions.
Use management liquidity commentary as a check on near-term funding and rating pressure.
Treat governance and control disclosures as qualitative checks rather than direct valuation drivers.
